governance.attested_by: neiso-54 extreme-day reliability drag session 2026-07-08 (branch claude/neiso-steamgas-ct-drag-d95pyn)
governance.note: neiso-54 = the neiso-53 keeper recipe (identical run_config, flags and the three winter fuel-security mechanisms) re-solved on the current data tree, with ONE structural correction that lives entirely in base data (reliability_floor_coeffs_NEISO.csv), so the recipe (CLI flags) is byte-unchanged and the only delta vs neiso-53 is the NEISO extreme-day reliability drag: (1) CT_PEAKER EVENING-RAMP DRAG (headline): CT_PEAKER now carries evening-windowed [15,21] tmax/netload limbs at floor_pct = commit_frac x min_stable (0.38) - the simple-cycle peakers' local-Resource-Adequacy commitment through the afternoon-evening net-load ramp, the hours their measured CAMPD CF genuinely rises with the driver (5 limbs enabled: Boston tmax+netload, Connecticut tmax+netload, North netload; each rho>=0.3, n>=30, commit_frac>baseline). It REPLACES the all-24h CT_PEAKER limbs scrubbed 2026-07-05 (which bound overnight where CT CF ~0, a rule-12 off-window bug): the evening window clears D-4 off-window (PASS) and lands CT profile_r 0.969/0.979/0.978 vs actual. CT_PEAKER is ~0.5-0.7% of ISO load (<2% materiality floor), so its 26-30% in-window forced share is reported-not-gated (rule 20 v2.1); C8 PASSES. (2) ST_GAS -> COMPONENT B CONSOLIDATION (rule 14/19): the lone 81 MW NEISO ST_GAS unit sits inside a 491 MW mixed CAMPD facility (code 546), so no clean pure-play commitment signal can be measured; its overnight reliability limbs ship as VISIBLE DISABLED placeholders (rule 12). With no enabled ST_GAS netload limb, run_calibration keeps ST_GAS inside the winter fuel-security must-run scope, so Component B now floors the model's 81 MW ST_GAS all-day on Nov-Mar cold days (WRP/IEP/OFSA posture) - ONE program-grounded mechanism for the ST_GAS phenomenon, replacing the contaminated all-24h netload limb it superseded (neiso-53 had Component B DROP ST_GAS because that netload limb was enabled; neiso-54 removes the limb so the program posture owns the class cleanly). RATIONALE (rule 1): both changes add/clean up REAL, forward-derivable market structure - the CT evening RA commitment the scrub had removed, now windowed correctly; and ST_GAS on a single grounded mechanism - with an IDENTICAL scored verdict to neiso-53 (C1 12/12 free 8/8 PASS, C3a/C3b commercial-band CAVEAT, C3c/C5b the same ledgered winter-scarcity caveats, C4/C5a PASS, C7 SKIPPED immaterial, C8 PASS) and NO winter degradation (C3c winter tail unchanged; ST_GAS is MORE committed in winter under Component B's all-day 0.40 posture than under the old 0.03 netload floor). Nothing is fit to a price/volume residual: the CT floor_pct is a measured online-share x a physical Pmin, honesty-gated (rho/n/commit>baseline), and it moves no scored metric because the class is immaterial - it is kept for structural faithfulness (rule 1), not to move the backcast. The C3c/C5b/C3a winter-scarcity and de-leak caveat families are UNCHANGED from neiso-53 (this drag neither closes nor worsens them).
governance.validation_note: Reproducible from the committed bundle: python scripts/run_neiso54_steamgas_ct_drag.py (the neiso-53 recipe re-solved with the committed reliability_floor_coeffs_NEISO.csv drag; --commitment unlocks the archived P2 the frozen neiso-53 keeper used, so the drag is the only delta). Coefficients regenerate from scripts/derive_neiso_steamgas_ct_drag.py (honesty-gated, NEISO-only). ABLATION TWIN: a fresh zero-forcing twin (--zero-forcing-ablation, same recipe, full 2023-2025 span) is registered alongside as 2026-07-08-neiso-54-steamgas-ct-ablation; audit_keepers.py E9 flags this bundle until it is linked. D-2 attribution (materiality-correct, sidecar): every forced class is IMMATERIAL and reported-not-gated - CT_PEAKER 69/51/30% of 0.5-0.7% -of-load energy, ST_GAS 28/84/65% of 0.1-0.3%, COAL 35/23/2% of <0.1% (rule 20 v2.1); C8 PASSES. D-4 off-window PASSES (the evening [15,21] window binds only in the CT ramp). Leave-one-year-out (rule 22): the scored verdict is IDENTICAL to neiso-53 every year - no criterion changes status due to the drag (no verdict flip), and the CT coefficients are a measured online-share x a physical Pmin re-derived only when the CAMPD/weather source updates (frozen against residuals, rule 23), so no value is fitted to a single year. Holdouts (2022, H1-2026, 2019) remain fully quarantined (rule 22); NEISO's locked-test one-shot STANDS on neiso-53 and is NOT re-scored for neiso-54.
governance.note_neiso54_ct_shape: CT_PEAKER C7/D-1: profile_r 0.969/0.979/0.978 (excellent), off-peak CV ratio 0.646/0.453/0.666 (2024 <0.5). entries.name: ST_GAS/CC_CHP measured-offer-band reach-ratio dependency (2026-07-06 addendum)
entries.where: results/calibration/neiso_stgas_netload (offer_curve_by_group ST_GAS + CC_CHP entries, same 72-scalar surface as the first ledger entry above)
entries.identification: derived-dependency (declares a coupling within already-counted scalars; not a new free parameter)
entries.source: The ST_GAS 0.79/0.85/0.89 and CC_CHP 1.15/1.17/1.19 bands are the NEISO-native CAMPD-measured marginal heat rate (ST_GAS 0.642/0.692/0.731; CC_CHP flat 0.94-0.97) multiplied by the NEISO-native CC reach ratio 1.223 (= CC_REGULAR econ_high 1.15 / native CC marginal HR 0.940). CC_REGULAR econ_high 1.15 is itself residual-identified (see the first ledger entry's offer_curve_by_group.value.CC_REGULAR.econ_high). So while the ST_GAS/CC_CHP bands are measured-grounded in level, the reach ratio that anchors them to the CC_REGULAR scale is not independent of that residual value.
entries.root_cause: wave-manager tranche review 2026-07-06 (#1498 deficiency 6, docs/handoffs/wave-manager-tranche-review-2026-07-06.md): dependency was undeclared at neiso-49's promotion. If CC_REGULAR econ_high (1.15) is ever re-identified (re-derived under a different residual fit), the reach ratio 1.223 changes, and the ST_GAS 0.79/0.85/0.89 and CC_CHP 1.15/1.17/1.19 bands re-derive with it — they are not independently anchored.

entries.citation: min_stable_pct 0.40 = subcritical steam-boiler turndown (Merrimack-class coal min-load ~40% nameplate); commit_frac 1.0 = the WRP/IEP fuel-secure steam fleet IS the program fleet; tmin_c -7C = NERC cold-weather forced-outage onset (~20 degF). Program driver: Winter Reliability Program FERC ER14-2407 -> IEP ER19-1428 -> OFSA. None tuned to the C1/C3c/C5b residual (rule 23 frozen). Component B BINDS on the immaterial fuel-secure COAL fleet (D-2 forced share 0.35/0.23/0.02 vs 0 in the twin; COAL <0.3% of ISO load, reported-not-gated per rule 20 v2.1, moves no scored metric); ST_GAS is dropped from Component B when the reliability netload limb is active (rule 24), so ST_GAS forced share is unchanged (owned by that limb).

entries.name: neiso_winter_fuel_inventory (Component A) + neiso_winter_fuel_start_fill_bbl
entries.citation: Nov-Mar oil-burn seasonal budget = start_fill x (1 + delivery_fills) / 5 months, MMBtu-correct over the oil-capable fleet (oil-primary + dual-fuel oil limb on switch hours). start_fill 2.8M bbl = Winter Reliability Program (FERC ER14-2407) 2014/15 low fleet oil-inventory target; delivery rate + tank autonomy from ISO-NE OFSA / WRP studies + EIA-860 (winter-fuel-inventory clean datatype). Forward-regenerable capacity/logistics quantities (rule 13), not measured receipts. Never tuned to the residual; monthly cap 9.79 M MMBtu is never approached (winter draw ~3.3 M/month).

entries.name: neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate + neiso_gas_derate_{t0_c,slope_per_c,cap}
entries.lineage_solves: adopted 2026-07-07 (G-24); <=13% cut on 8 cold-peak hours, moves no price
entries.citation: Temperature-dependent forced-outage of non-dual-fuel gas-CC/CT: frac = clip(slope*(t0-TMIN),0,cap) on the winter cold-snap peak hours, keyed to NEISO load-weighted daily TMIN. cap 0.20 = NERC/FERC Winter Storm Elliott (gas fuel-supply ~20% of unplanned outages, largest forced-out category); t0 -7C = NERC cold-onset; slope 0.018 = cap/(t0 - T_extreme). Forward-reproducible from pinned/forecast TMIN, condition-responsive, NOT fitted to the number of >$300 hours (produces zero here).
